title: Community laundry drying rack access
valued_outcome: Residents can find usable rack space without disturbing another resident's laundry.
success_measure: During the stipulated busy period, at least nine of ten arrivals locate usable space within three minutes without moving another load.

hard_constraints.text: No resident may move another resident's laundry.
Keep the existing four racks and room layout.
Any per-load recording must take no more than one minute.
Do not record names or apartment numbers.

incumbent: Residents choose rack space on arrival. Existing partial mechanisms are paper arrival-time tags attached to loads and a wall calendar showing requested drying windows. Tags show when a load was placed, while calendar entries describe intentions. No one routinely reconciles the two.

observations.text: Synthetic arrival log: eight of 20 arrivals initially found all racks occupied.
Synthetic tag audit: seven of 18 tags remained attached after their laundry was removed.
Synthetic calendar sample: five of twelve requested windows had no corresponding arrival.
Synthetic resident diary: three residents described usable space obscured by empty tagged hangers.
Synthetic timing sheet: adding an arrival-time tag took 25 to 45 seconds in six trials.
Synthetic room log: two racks became empty within ten minutes of each other on one evening.

unknowns: How often tags are removed promptly.
Whether planned windows influence actual arrival choices.
resources: Existing tags, calendar, pencils and four racks.
changeable_assumptions: Arrival time is the only load state recorded.
Requested windows are accepted without confirmation.
provenance: Entirely authored synthetic preservation fixture; supplied sources are stipulations, not field observations or tested effects.
